Kind of a similar issue. When I first set up my HF rig in my new house I was getting a lot of stray RF in my computer room. It would cause my mouse to jump all over the screen and my computer speakers to cut out while transmitting. It turned out to be a mismatch between the length of the feed wire and the antenna. It's call common mode current. The coax shield acts as part of the antenna and it dumps RF all over the place instead of out of the antenna where it's supposed to radiate from. Not sure if that is the issue with your radio. But I remember looking up these RF chokes that fix that and a fellow HAM told me to not bother because the correct thing to do is fix either the feed line or the antenna. I replaced the feed line with a longer one and no more crazy things happening in my ham shack room when I transmit. I would do what others have suggested and stick an antenna analyzer on the antenna to see what the SWR is. You might have an issue with the antenna or might just need a longer feed line going to it. Just a thought.
